title: ComBeautify: Leveraging Code Change Summaries for Conventional Commit Generation
title_zh: ComBeautify：利用代码变更摘要生成规范化提交

paragraphs.en: Modern software development extensively relies on Version Control Systems (VCS) such as Git to track changes and facilitate collaboration. While commit messages are crucial for conveying developer intent, they do not directly affect program functionality; as a result, developers often lack motivation to write meaningful commit messages. The Conventional Commits Specification (CCS) addresses this issue by introducing a structured format and guidelines that help developers express the intent of a change, improving clarity, and enabling automation. Despite these specifications, developers frequently struggle to express intent while adhering to the format. In particular, they may misclassify commits due to the large number of possible categories or the lack of project-specific guidance. In this paper, we introduce ComBeautify, an approach that automatically generates CCS-compliant commit messages. We use a hybrid approach that leverages context-preserving summarization of Git diffs with large language models (LLMs) to improve commit classification accuracy under CCS. Rather than relying on manually curated category definitions, we learn them from historical commits. We also propose a method for automatically generating the CCS description component.

paragraphs.en: Our extensive empirical evaluation across 13 languages, 6,500 open-source repositories, and over 20 million commits demonstrates long-term insights into CCS adoption trends, revealing increasing compliance. Our evaluation on twenty popular repositories reveals the limitations of approaches guided by generic category definitions, and shows that ComBeautify, when trained on project-specific data, outperforms baseline approaches by up to 3 × \times in some cases. Additionally, using a dataset of 2,000 manually curated commits, we validate our summarization approach, achieving up to 95.25% accuracy and surpassing baseline methods. These findings emphasize the need for adaptable, context-aware AI methods for commit classification and generation of CCS-compliant commit messages.

paragraphs.en: Version Control Systems (VCS) such as Git, Subversion, and Mercurial have become an integral part of the modern software development workflow. They allow multiple developers to collaborate on a project, keeping track of the modifications to the codebase. A commit is a fundamental operation that captures a snapshot of changes made to the codebase at a particular point. In addition to changes in the codebase, a commit contains additional information such as the author of the change, the time and date of the commit, and a commit message typically written in a natural language. The commit message is primarily used to express the developer’s intent behind the change and to communicate it with other developers.

paragraphs.en: To this end, Tian et al. (2022) propose a criterion for a high-quality commit message, emphasizing that it should consist of both ‘what’ (summary of changes in the commit) and ‘why’ (reasons for making those changes). Their analysis of five open source projects finds that 44% of the commit messages lack essential information, of these 44% contain only ‘what’, 12% only contain ‘why’, and 4% contain neither ‘why’ nor ‘what’. This highlights a prevalent issue in modern software development: writing a highly effective commit message. This can be due to developers deprioritizing writing high-quality messages due to time constraints and the belief that changes are self-explanatory. In addition to this, there is a lack of clear guidelines on what constitutes a good commit message in many projects, and distributed teams with varying practices further contribute to this inconsistency. These challenges highlight the need for an automated tool to help developers write highly effective commit messages.

paragraphs.en: The lack of a standardized commit format often leads to fragmented and ambiguous commit messages, hindering effective repository management and code understanding. To address this, the Conventional Commits Specification (CCS) introduces a standardized, project-agnostic format. It specifies that a commit message should be structured as <type>[optional scope]: <description> , followed by an optional body and footer. For example, consider the commit 3839cfb taken from the GitHub repository of Angular shown in Figure 2 (and abbreviated here for brevity). The <type> in this case is fix and the <description> is “Routed components never inherit RouterOutlet EnvironmentInjector” . The commit fixes a bug in response to an issue report. The intention of the developer is made clear through the use of the fix type and a one-line description to explain the change. router represents the [scope] which provides additional context to the type. The remaining part of the commit message contains the body and the last line represents the footer.

paragraphs.en: To this end, this paper aims to automatically synthesize a structured conventional commit message from a non-compliant commit. We propose an approach that employs Large Language Models (LLMs) to summarize commit changes and combines this summary with the original commit message to generate a complete CCS-compliant commit. Specifically, we use two fine-tuned LLMs to generate the CCS type and description, respectively. As a result, our approach produces an informative, structured commit message that complies with the CCS specification. The bottom part of Figure 1 shows an example of a CCS-compliant output generated by our approach.
paragraphs.zh: 为此，本文旨在从不合规的提交中自动合成结构化的约定式提交信息。 我们提出一种方法，利用大语言模型（LLM）总结提交变更，并将该摘要与原始提交信息结合，以生成完整的符合 CCS 规范的提交。 具体而言，我们使用两个经过微调的 LLM 分别生成 CCS 的类型和描述。 因此，我们的方法能够生成符合 CCS 规范且信息丰富、结构化的提交信息。 图 1 的底部展示了我们的方法生成的符合 CCS 规范的输出示例。

paragraphs.en: A key insight of our approach is that in practice CCS conventions are adapted to project-level specifics. Whereas prior work on commit classification typically targets a predefined, manually curated set of commit types ( Zeng et al., 2024 ) , our approach automatically learns each project’s own conventions from its commit history, and uses them to synthesize both the type and the description of a compliant message. We demonstrate that such project-specific learning outperforms generalized models for commit classification and commit message generation.

paragraphs.en: The primary elements of a commit consist of one or more file changes along with a message that describes the nature of the change. These file changes are typically represented as file-based differences (diffs), which capture modifications at the code level. To this end, effectively capturing the developer’s intent behind a commit presents two key challenges:

sents.en: The primary elements of a commit consist of one or more file changes along with a message that describes the nature of the change.
sents.zh: 提交的主要组成部分包括一个或多个文件更改，以及一条描述更改性质的提交信息。

sents.en: These file changes are typically represented as file-based differences (diffs), which capture modifications at the code level.
sents.zh: 这些文件更改通常以基于文件的差异（diff）形式表示，用于捕捉代码层面的修改。

sents.en: To this end, effectively capturing the developer’s intent behind a commit presents two key challenges:
sents.zh: 为此，有效捕捉提交背后开发者的意图面临两个关键挑战：

paragraphs.en: File-level diffs of commits can often be arbitrarily large (the average character length of a diff in our dataset is 20,324), making them difficult to process comprehensively.
paragraphs.zh: 提交的文件级差异往往可能非常大（我们数据集中差异的平均字符长度为 20,324），这使得难以对其进行全面处理。

paragraphs.en: The mandatory components of a CCS, namely, the type and description, are generally expressed in natural language (e.g., English). Therefore, relying solely on file-based diffs, which emphasize code-level changes, is suboptimal for tasks involving natural language generation.
paragraphs.zh: CCS 的强制性组成部分，即类型和描述，通常以自然语言（例如英语）表达。 因此，仅依赖以文件为基础的差异比较（其侧重于代码层面的变更），对于涉及自然语言生成的任务而言并非最优选择。

sents.zh: CCS 的强制性组成部分，即类型和描述，通常以自然语言（例如英语）表达。

sents.en: Therefore, relying solely on file-based diffs, which emphasize code-level changes, is suboptimal for tasks involving natural language generation.
sents.zh: 因此，仅依赖以文件为基础的差异比较（其侧重于代码层面的变更），对于涉及自然语言生成的任务而言并非最优选择。

paragraphs.en: To address these challenges, our key insight is to generate a natural language summary of the diff and use this summary as input instead of directly providing code-level diffs.
paragraphs.zh: 为了解决这些挑战，我们的关键洞察是生成代码差异（diff）的自然语言摘要，并使用该摘要作为输入，而不是直接提供代码层面的差异（diff）。

The green digits prefixed with a + + indicate the number of lines added, while the red digits prefixed with a − - indicate the number of lines deleted. In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable code-understanding capabilities ( Feng et al., 2020 ; Nam et al., 2024 ; Anand et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2021 ) . Accordingly, we adopt an in-context learning approach to generate natural language summaries of code diffs. Specifically, the computed diff is tokenized and, together with a carefully constructed prompt and a few examples, is provided as input to LLM s ​ u ​ m ​ m ​ a ​ r ​ y \text{LLM}_{summary} , which generates a brief summary S S (in our case, the average summary length is 688 characters, a 30x reduction from the original code diff).
paragraphs.zh: 为了有效，摘要必须捕捉代码变更差异中的关键内容。 近年来，大语言模型（LLM）展现出了出色的代码理解能力（Feng et al., 2020；Nam et al., 2024；Anand et al., 2024；Chen et al., 2021）。 因此，我们采用上下文学习方法来生成代码差异的自然语言摘要。 具体而言，计算得到的差异会被分词，并与精心构建的提示词以及少量示例一起作为输入提供给 \text{LLM}_{summary}，由其生成简短摘要 S S（在我们的案例中，摘要的平均长度为 688 个字符，相比原始代码差异缩减了 30 倍）。

paragraphs.en: While a diff captures code-level changes, the commit message typically conveys the developer’s intent in natural language. Although there is no enforced limit on commit-message length, in practice these messages are quite short (the average length in our dataset is 91 characters). Therefore, we perform no additional processing on the message and simply append it to the diff summary obtained earlier. We refer to this combined representation as the commit-intent representation ( ℂ \mathbb{C} in Algorithm 1 ).
paragraphs.zh: 虽然 diff 记录的是代码层面的变更，但提交信息通常以自然语言传达开发者的意图。 尽管提交信息的长度没有强制限制，但实际上这些信息相当短（在我们数据集中平均长度为 91 个字符）。 因此，我们对提交信息不做额外处理，只是将其追加到先前获得的 diff 摘要中。 我们将这种组合表示称为提交意图表示（算法 1 中的 ℂ \mathbb{C} ）。

paragraphs.en: The commit-intent-representation ℂ \mathbb{C} serves as the primary input for generating the mandatory components of a CCS-compliant message: the type and description . We fine-tune two separate LLMs, one for type generation and the other for description generation. We decouple these tasks because they require different levels of abstraction. Generating a single-word type typically requires understanding the developer’s high-level intent. In contrast, generating a multi-word description demands a fine-grained understanding of the semantic impact of the change. For both fine-tuning approaches, we use commits that comply with CCS as input. We describe each task in more detail below.
paragraphs.zh: 提交意图表示 ℂ \mathbb{C} 作为生成符合 CCS 规范消息的必需组件的主要输入：即类型和描述。 我们微调两个独立的 LLM，一个用于类型生成，另一个用于描述生成。 我们将这两个任务解耦，因为它们需要不同层次的抽象。 生成单个单词的类型通常需要理解开发者的高层意图。 相比之下，生成多单词的描述需要对变更的语义影响有细粒度的理解。 对于两种微调方法，我们都使用符合 CCS 规范的提交作为输入。 我们将在下文更详细地描述每个任务。

paragraphs.en: The Conventional Commit Specification defines a type as a mandatory element of the commit message. A type, a single word according to the specification, signifies the kind of change made in the commit. The type can be optionally accompanied by a scope, which provides additional context. The focus of our work is to generate only the mandatory components of a CCS, and as a result, generating the scope is not considered in this paper.
paragraphs.zh: 约定式提交规范将类型定义为提交信息中的必填元素。 根据该规范，类型是一个单词，表示该次提交所做变更的类别。 类型可以可选地带有一个范围，以提供额外的上下文。 我们的工作重点是仅生成约定式提交（CCS）的必填组成部分，因此本文不考虑范围的生成。

paragraphs.en: The specification recommends, but does not strictly enforce, any type except two: feat and fix . The feat type is used when a commit adds a new feature, while fix is used for bug-fixing commits. The remaining types do not have formally specified definitions. Additionally, developers are free to introduce new custom types beyond the standard CCS types. The reasons for project-specific definitions and custom types are manifold. First, some projects have domain-specific nuances that are not captured by standard categories. Second, projects may rely on specific automated workflows based on internally agreed-upon types.
paragraphs.zh: 该规范推荐（但并不严格强制）除两种类型之外的所有类型：feat 和 fix。 feat 类型用于提交新功能的提交，而 fix 用于修复缺陷的提交。 其余类型没有正式规定的定义。 此外，开发者可以自由引入标准 CCS 类型之外的自定义新类型。 采用项目特定定义和自定义类型的原因是多方面的。 首先，某些项目具有标准类别无法涵盖的领域特定细微差别。 其次，项目可能依赖基于内部商定类型的特定自动化工作流。

paragraphs.en: This challenge is evident in how common development activities are categorized. To illustrate this, we analyzed our dataset for commits related to two frequent tasks: resolving merge conflicts and updating dependencies. For each task, commits were identified by searching commit messages for predefined phrases (e.g., “fix merge conflict” and “resolve conflicts” for merge conflicts; “update dependencies” and “bump deps” for dependency updates). Table 1 presents the distribution of CCS types assigned to commits performing these tasks, focusing on five popular types: feat , fix , chore , build , and refactor . Results demonstrate that common development activities are inconsistently categorized across various CCS types. Such dispersion for well-defined tasks indicates ambiguity in CCS type selection and highlights the need for automated assistance.
paragraphs.zh: 这一挑战在常见开发活动的分类方式中表现得十分明显。 为了说明这一点，我们分析了数据集中与两类常见任务相关的提交：解决合并冲突和更新依赖。 对于每类任务，我们通过在提交信息中搜索预定义短语来识别相关提交（例如，合并冲突对应“fix merge conflict”和“resolve conflicts”；依赖更新对应“update dependencies”和“bump deps”）。 表 1 展示了执行这些任务的提交所被分配的 CCS 类型的分布，重点关注五种常用类型：feat、fix、chore、build 和 refactor。 结果表明，常见开发活动在不同 CCS 类型之间的分类并不一致。 对于定义明确的任务尚且出现如此分散的情况，说明 CCS 类型的选择存在模糊性，也凸显了自动化辅助的必要性。

One of the major challenges for an approach that generates a type is the widespread use of custom types (there exist more than 215K distinct types in our dataset, Section 3.3 ). paragraphs.en: To overcome this limitation, we propose to learn project-specific CCS types from historical commits. Our key insight is that while the semantics of a given type tend to remain consistent within a single project, they can vary significantly across different projects. Additionally, a project-specific approach is not limited to a custom set of predefined types.

paragraphs.en: We develop an automated pipeline to collect and process commit-level data from these repositories, focusing on activity from January 2017 onward. The pipeline initially attempts shallow cloning to minimize storage and network overhead ( git clone --shallow-since ). If this fails, we use fallback mechanisms, including full cloning and GitHub’s REST API, with rotating tokens to mitigate rate limits. As a result, the pipeline yields approximately 21.5 million non-merge commits from 6,500 repositories, constituting our experimental dataset. Within this dataset, we identify CCS-compliant commits using regular expressions to detect messages that adhere to the <type>: <description> structure, optionally followed by a body.
paragraphs.zh: 我们开发了一个自动化流水线，从这些仓库中收集并处理提交级别的数据，重点关注2017年1月以来的活动。 该流水线首先尝试浅克隆以最小化存储和网络开销（git clone --shallow-since）。 如果失败，我们会使用回退机制，包括完整克隆和 GitHub 的 REST API，并通过轮换令牌来缓解速率限制。 因此，该流水线从6,500个仓库中获得了约2150万个非合并提交，构成了我们的实验数据集。 在该数据集中，我们使用正则表达式识别符合 CCS 规范的提交，以检测遵循 <type>: <description> 结构、其后可选跟有正文的消息。

paragraphs.en: To assess the prevalence of conventional commits among developers, we conduct a large-scale empirical analysis of adoption trends across open-source projects.
paragraphs.zh: 为了评估常规提交在开发者中的普及程度，我们对开源项目的采用趋势进行了大规模的实证分析。

paragraphs.en: Our analysis reveals that, out of 20.76 million commits in our dataset, about 5.1 million are CCS commits, accounting for 24.58%. of the total, authored by over 600,000 unique contributors.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的分析显示，在我们数据集的 2076 万次提交中，约有 510 万次是 CCS 提交，占总数的 24.58%，由超过 60 万名独立贡献者完成。

paragraphs.en: Of the 6,500 repositories present in our dataset, we assess CCS adoption by calculating repository-level compliance as the percentage of commits adhering to the Conventional Commits specification. Our analysis reveals that 1247 repositories (19.2%) exhibit at least 70% compliance, with 991 (15.2%) surpassing 80%, 708 (10.9%) exceeding 90%, and 482 (7.4%) demonstrating compliance above 95%.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们数据集中包含的 6,500 个仓库中，我们通过计算仓库级合规率（即遵循 Conventional Commits 规范的提交所占百分比）来评估 CCS 的采用情况。 我们的分析显示，1247 个仓库（19.2%）的合规率达到至少 70%，其中 991 个（15.2%）超过 80%，708 个（10.9%）超过 90%，482 个（7.4%）的合规率高于 95%。

sents.en: Of the 6,500 repositories present in our dataset, we assess CCS adoption by calculating repository-level compliance as the percentage of commits adhering to the Conventional Commits specification.
sents.zh: 在我们数据集中包含的 6,500 个仓库中，我们通过计算仓库级合规率（即遵循 Conventional Commits 规范的提交所占百分比）来评估 CCS 的采用情况。

sents.en: Our analysis reveals that 1247 repositories (19.2%) exhibit at least 70% compliance, with 991 (15.2%) surpassing 80%, 708 (10.9%) exceeding 90%, and 482 (7.4%) demonstrating compliance above 95%.

paragraphs.en: We also examine year-wise CCS adoption from 2017 onward across all commits in our dataset. In 2017, 16.3% of commits were CCS-compliant. By 2025, this proportion had increased to 35.9%, representing more than a twofold rise over eight years. This trajectory indicates a consistent increase in adherence to the CCS specification over time.
paragraphs.zh: 我们还考察了自2017年起数据集中所有提交按年份的CCS采用情况。 2017年，16.3%的提交符合CCS规范。 到2025年，这一比例上升至35.9%，在八年间增长超过一倍。 这一轨迹表明，对CCS规范的遵循程度随时间持续提升。

paragraphs.en: We further analyze CCS adoption across programming languages to assess whether certain ecosystems exhibit stronger adherence. Figure 4 summarizes the results. TypeScript projects show the highest average CCS compliance (53.9%), followed by Go (44.4%), Rust (38.9%), and JavaScript (34.9%). Dart, C, C++, Python, Shell, and Kotlin exhibit moderate adoption, whereas Java, C#, and Swift show comparatively lower compliance rates.
paragraphs.zh: 我们进一步分析了CCS在不同编程语言中的采用情况，以评估某些生态系统是否表现出更强的遵循度。 图4总结了结果。 TypeScript项目显示出最高的平均CCS合规性（53.9%），其次是Go（44.4%）、Rust（38.9%）和JavaScript（34.9%）。 Dart、C、C++、Python、Shell和Kotlin呈现出中等程度的采用率，而Java、C#和Swift的合规率相对较低。

paragraphs.en: To understand the current landscape of the varied types that developers adopt during a commit, we analyze all CCS commits and check their types. The ten most frequent CCS types are fix (13.4%), chore (10.3%), feat (8.3%), docs (4.2%), refactor (2.7%), build (2.6%), test (1.7%), ci (1.3%), doc (1.1%), tests (0.8%) We find that CCS types form a long-tailed distribution. In total, there are over 215,000 distinct types. We find that due to the lack of restrictions by the specification there is an extensive use of custom CCS types.
paragraphs.zh: 为了了解开发者在提交时采用的各种类型的现状，我们分析了所有 CCS 提交并检查其类型。 最常见的十种 CCS 类型是 fix（13.4%）、chore（10.3%）、feat（8.3%）、docs（4.2%）、refactor（2.7%）、build（2.6%）、test（1.7%）、ci（1.3%）、doc（1.1%）、tests（0.8%）。我们发现 CCS 类型呈现长尾分布。 总共有超过 21.5 万种不同的类型。 我们发现，由于规范缺乏限制，自定义 CCS 类型被大量使用。

paragraphs.en: Overall, our empirical study confirms rising CCS adoption across languages and repositories and highlights diversity of CCS types used in individual projects. Together, these findings motivate the need for an automated approach to aid developers in formulating project-aligned CCS types and commit messages.
paragraphs.zh: 总体而言，我们的实证研究证实了 CCS 在不同语言和代码仓库中的采用率不断上升，并突出了单个项目中所使用的 CCS 类型的多样性。 这些发现共同表明，需要一种自动化方法来帮助开发者制定与项目相匹配的 CCS 类型和提交信息。

paragraphs.en: The empirical study of Section 3.3 show a steady increase in CCS adoption by developers. The findings indicate that although about 19% of repositories have at least 70% CCS compliance, there are still a large number of commits that do not comply with CCS. To this end, we investigate whether ComBeautify can automatically transform unstructured commits into fully CCS-compliant commits.

paragraphs.en: One of the major challenges faced by developers during a commit is deciding on the required type. To this end, we propose automatically inferring project-specific types and compare its applicability to five other approaches mentioned below. For this experiment, we select twenty popular GitHub repositories (based on ✩ count) from our experimental setup with differing levels of adherence to CCS. For each project, we randomly select 2000 commits of which 1400 are used for training, 200 for validation, and 400 for evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 开发人员在提交过程中面临的主要挑战之一是确定所需的类型。 为此，我们提出自动推断项目特定的类型，并将其适用性与下文提到的其他五种方法进行比较。 对于本实验，我们从实验设置中选取了二十个流行的 GitHub 仓库（基于 ✩ 数量），这些仓库对 CCS 的遵循程度各不相同。 对于每个项目，我们随机选择 2000 个提交，其中 1400 个用于训练，200 个用于验证，400 个用于评估。

sents.en: One of the major challenges faced by developers during a commit is deciding on the required type.
sents.zh: 开发人员在提交过程中面临的主要挑战之一是确定所需的类型。

sents.en: To this end, we propose automatically inferring project-specific types and compare its applicability to five other approaches mentioned below.
sents.zh: 为此，我们提出自动推断项目特定的类型，并将其适用性与下文提到的其他五种方法进行比较。

sents.en: For this experiment, we select twenty popular GitHub repositories (based on ✩ count) from our experimental setup with differing levels of adherence to CCS.

sents.en: For each project, we randomly select 2000 commits of which 1400 are used for training, 200 for validation, and 400 for evaluation.

paragraphs.en: CCS does not provide explicit definitions for the types used in commit messages. As a result, developers often struggle to correctly assign appropriate types. Manually providing definitions for these types is a time-consuming and non-scalable approach, particularly for large or rapidly evolving projects.

These finding demonstrate the generalizability of ComBeautify and the applicability in a development workflow.

paragraphs.en: We perform an experiment to check if the commit-intent-representation of ComBeautify is useful in detecting commits as breaking change. For this, we fine-tune a local model using commit-intent-representation selected from the top-20 projects of Table 2 . To reflect real-world commit distributions, where breaking changes are relatively rare, we construct dataset using 1:3 ratio of breaking to non-breaking commits. For evaluation, we remove any hints (e.g., remove ! ! from type ! ! ) present in a commit message about the breaking change and compare the performance of a general-purpose model (Gemini 2.0) and our fine-tuned model in identifying if a commit is a breaking change. We find that both models perform relatively well where Gemini achieves an accuracy of 83.25% while our model achieves 88% (despite its relatively smaller size). The result demonstrates the usefulness of commit-intent-representation and also the applicability of a specialized model in automatically identifying a breaking change that may aid developers.

Instead, atomic commit that makes one logical change to the codebase is encouraged.

paragraphs.en: In this experiment, we randomly select a sample of 100,000 commits stratified over repositories that adhere to CCS, and 100,000 that do not, drawn from our experimental dataset. The analysis reveals that the average number of lines per commit is 466 for CCS-compliant commits and 679 for non-compliant ones. The results show that the commits that follow CCS are on average 30% smaller in size. These findings suggest that developers who adhere to CCS are more inclined to make smaller, more incremental code changes, further reinforcing the potential benefits of CCS.

paragraphs.en: As an ablation study, we evaluate if performing an additional step to summarize the code differences affects the performance of ComBeautify. To this end, we compare ComBeautify to two other approaches. The first approach is a prior work by Zeng et al. (2024) (referred to as Non-summarized), that uses an LLM fine-tuned directly on unprocessed commits to classify CCS types; The second approach uses zero-shot inference using the GPT-4o model. In the latter case, we use prompting techniques to generate types from the GPT-4o without any additional learning involved. Since the approach proposed in prior work ( Zeng et al., 2024 ) also incorporates manual definitions of type, for this experiment, we provide the manual definitions as part of the input for all of the approaches to ensure fair comparison.

paragraphs.en: CCS is a relatively recent proposal and its adoption is evolving rapidly. Consequently, the trends observed in our current analysis may not remain valid in the future. To address this threat, we take a long-term view of the trend starting from 2017 through 2025. Our project-specific evaluation is based on twenty open-source projects, which may not constitute a representative sample. We address this concern by choosing popular and diverse projects each with at least 30K GitHub stars. To identify if a commit complies with CCS, we rely on the structure as specified by CCS. However, it is possible for commits to follow the prescribed format without fully adhering to the intent of the specification. To reduce the implications of this threat, we manually inspect a sample of commits and find them to be CCS compliant. We conduct our experiments utilizing specific versions of LLMs. LLMs are known to hallucinate results which can have an impact on our results. Additionally, any future updates to these models can adversely impact our findings. To address this threat, we preserve the findings of our experiments. LLMs are also known to be sensitive to prompts and as a result, the a major threat for our approach comes from crafting the prompts.

paragraphs.en: Our work on generating CCS-compliant commits contributes to an active research field of automated Commit Message Generation (CMG), a functionality now widely integrated into code editors as part of AI code assistance. CMG aims to assist developers by automatically producing informative commit messages, and incorporates various retrieval-based and learning-based techniques ( Zhang et al., 2024b ) . Recently, large language models (LLMs) have been actively applied to CMG. For instance, Xue et al. (2024) studied the use of LLMs for CMG and proposed ERICommiter, a framework that curates and retrieves relevant historical commit examples to effectively guide LLMs via in-context learning to generate high-quality commit messages. Similarly, Zhang et al. (2024a) proposed REACT, a retrieval-based framework that finds exemplar diff-message pairs to guide LLMs during CMG. The efficacy of in-context learning for LLM-based CMG was further empirically investigated by Wu et al. (2025) , who studied the impact of various prompts and demonstration settings across different LLMs and datasets. Other research has focused on enabling LLMs to leverage richer context beyond code diffs or simple exemplars. Li et al. (2024) introduced Omniscient Message Generator, which treats CMG as a knowledge-intensive reasoning task and employs an LLM to incorporate diverse software context (e.g., issue reports, pull requests) for generating more comprehensive commit messages. Eliseeva et al. (2023) investigated history-aware commit message completion. This use of past commit history aligns with our intuition behind generating project-specific CCS messages. Compared to our work, these CMG approaches do not adhere to the structured CCS specification; however, the proposed techniques for richer contextual and historical understanding could potentially improve generation of CCS descriptions.

paragraphs.en: The first systematic research focused specifically on Conventional Commits Specification (CCS) is conducted by Zeng et al. (2024) . The work studies CCS adoption, identifies challenges developers face when selecting CCS types, and proposes an LLM-based approach to classify commits into ten predefined CCS types. In contrast, our paper focuses on the generation of CCS-compliant commit types and descriptions. Furthermore, while Zeng et al. (2024) relies on a manually curated list of CCS types, our study demonstrates the importance of project-specific conventions, showing that models fine-tuned on project-specific data outperform generalized models. Additionally, we include a considerably larger analysis of CCS adoption, based on over 20 million commits, and provide case studies that highlight real-world benefits of using CCS.

paragraphs.en: Version control systems are central to modern software development, enabling collaboration and tracking code changes. The recently introduced Conventional Commit Specification (CCS) enforces a structured commit. The aim of ComBeautify is to automatically synthesize a complete structured commit given a code change and a natural language description. We address the fundamental challenge faced by developers in classifying commits leveraging two key insights. First, instead of using code differences directly, we propose to use a summary of the change. Second, instead of relying on manual annotations of commits, our approach automatically learns from historical commits. Our evaluation on real-world projects shows improvements in predicting the correct CCS type over an approach that uses manual annotation of definitions. Additionally, for generating the description, our approach outperforms two larger general-purpose models. We envision ComBeautify being used by developers to alleviate some of the challenges of correctly assigning a class to a commit. Beyond generating the type and description of a commit, future efforts could focus on generating the body as well. Additionally, extending ComBeautify to generate the scope alongside the type for a CCS commit represents another potential direction worth investigating.
